By order dated 4-5-98 District Magistrate, Chittagong detained the detenu Suranjit Barua (Labu) in exercise of power under section 3(2) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 for 30 days from the date of service of the order which was received by the detenue on 5-5-98. It appears that earlier on 9-4-98 detenu Suranjit Barna (Labu) was arrested by police from Nandan Kanan area of Chittaganj town on the allegation that he along with others assembled there to create terror in the area as on the previous night there was exchange of fire between terrorist groups at that place. Police made GD Entry No. 508 of dated 9-4-98 over the arrest of the said detenue along with others from the said area. In Criminal Misc. Case No. 1848 of 98 learned Sessions Judge granted ad interim bail for 2 weeks to the detenu on 27-4-98.But could not be released as he was also shown arrested in connection with another case Thereafter on 4-5-98 Sessions Judge granted bail to the detenu for 1 month in Criminal Misc Case No. 1901 of 9. But instead of releasing the detenu on the basis of the said order he was served, with the order of detention dated 4-5-98, Being aggrieved by the same his elder brother moved this court with an application under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule rom the supplementary affidavit It appears that Government extended the detention of the detenu for further period of 3 months with effect from 3-6-98 by order dated 31-5-98. 

 7. In the case of Md Suba Miah and another vs. Government of Bangladesh (Criminal Misc Case No.  818 of91) disposed of on 13-2-92 this question was raised and one of us who was a party to that judgment differed with the Presiding Judge of the Bench disposing of the said Rule. In the dissenting opinion expressed in the judgment after discussing the is provisions of sub-section (3) of section 491 of the Code and decisions in the case of Ranabir Pal Singh vs. Emperor reported in AIR 1949 Bombay 161, Md  Anowar vs. Crown reported in PW 1955 Lahore 585;  Emperor vs. Vimala Bai Desh Pande reported in AIR /946 (PC) 123; Ranbir Das vs. Secretary Ministry of  Home Affairs reported in 28 DLR 48; Emperor vs.  Shibnath Banerjee reported in AIR /946 (PC) 159;  Sultanara Begum vs. Secretary Ministry of Home  Affairs reported in 38 DLR 93 it was held: "when the  order of detention is purported to be one under the  Special Powers Act this court has power to examine  the materials produced to satisfy itself as to whether the order is one within the meaning and scope of the  same and if on such examination of the detention is illegal or improper then in an application under  section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure sub-section (3) of the said section will not be a bar to release the detenu from custody. Another Division Bench in the case of Pearu Mahammad vs State reported in 44 DLR 603 repelled the contention that scope of section 491 CrPC is limited and narrower than that of Article 102 of the Constitution. 

 9. Let us now examine the materials produced by the State in support of the detention of the detenu. From the file produced by the learned Assistant Attorney-General in pursuance of our direction we find that the file contains the following documents (1) A type written statement signed by the Deputy Commissioner of Metropolitan Police, Special Branch, Chittagong on 12-5-98 (2) Order dated 4-5-98 issued by the District Magistrate detaining the detenu Suranjit Barna (Labu) for 3(days under section 3(2) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 (3) Grounds of detention served on the detenu on 10-5-98 (4) An order of the Government dated 31-5-98 extending the detention of the detenu for 3 months with effect from 3-6-98. From the aforesaid statement dated 12-5-98 it appears that detenu was arrested on the basis of General Diary No.508 dated 9-4-98 under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he is locally known as a terrorist but in the grounds dated 10-5-98 detenu has been termed as a notorious terrorist, anti-social or anti-State element and a donation monger. He has also been termed as a member of the gang of smuggler and kidnappers. It has also been stated that he was a dangerous and terrible person and for [car of members of his gang nobody dared to raise objection against his terrorist activities and to give evidence in court against him. In support of the allegations noticed above there is no report by any police personnel either working in the local police station or in the Intelligence Branch or CID. In such circumstances in the absence of any supporting materials merely because petitioner has been termed a dangerous and terrible terrorist he cannot be detained in custody as there was no materials to justify the District- Magistrate or 'the Government that his detention is required under the provision of section of the Special Powers Act. We are satisfied that Government has failed to justify the detention of the detenu Suranjit Barua (Labu). So we are of the view   that the said detenu is being detained illegally or improperly and not in accordance with the requirement of section 3 of the Special Powers Act and, as such sub-section (3) of section 491 of the Code cannot stand as a bar to declare his detention as illegal. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.  Detention of the detenu Surunjit Barua (Labu) son of late SM Barua of 7, Abedin Colony, Love Lane, Police Station-Kotwali, District Chittagong now detained in Chittagong District Jail is declared illegal. Let him be set at liberty forthwith if not wanted in connection with any other case.
